about: Canonicalisation vectors for KERNEL-SPEC §2: a document, the exact RFC 8785 bytes it canonicalises to, and the sha256 of those bytes. The canonical strings are written by hand and reviewed; the digest is the sha256 of the canonical string, which a reader can check with 'printf %s <canonical> | sha256sum'.

encoding.note: JSON cannot spell every value the canonicaliser accepts, so a single-key object with one of these tags stands for the value named. Anything else is itself.
encoding.$int: int(<string>) -- for integers JSON itself cannot carry exactly
encoding.$float: float(<string>) -- only ever used in a rejection vector
encoding.$tuple: tuple(<array>) -- only ever used as a rejected mapping key
encoding.$pairs: a mapping built from [key, value] pairs, so keys can be non-strings

vectors.name: empty-object
vectors.why: An empty document is a document: it canonicalises and carries a digest.

vectors.name: key-order-and-nesting
vectors.why: Object keys are sorted at every depth; array order is never touched.

vectors.name: nfc-value-composed
vectors.why: The composed spelling of a string value is the canonical one.

vectors.name: nfd-value-decomposed
vectors.why: The decomposed spelling of the same value canonicalises to the same bytes as nfc-value-composed -- and therefore to the same digest.

vectors.name: nfd-key-decomposed
vectors.why: Normalisation applies to keys as well as values (KERNEL-SPEC §2.1).

vectors.name: key-coercion
vectors.why: PyYAML yields bool/int/null keys; they are coerced to their JSON spelling, then sorted as the strings they became. The int key here is 2 rather than 1 because Python's own dict would have merged an int 1 key with the True key before the canonicaliser ever saw them.

vectors.name: decimal-keeps-its-scale
vectors.why: A Decimal is a string at its declared scale, never a JSON number.

vectors.name: decimal-scale-is-part-of-the-value
vectors.why: The same number at a different declared scale is a different canonical document -- and a different digest from decimal-keeps-its-scale.

vectors.name: decimal-negative-zero-folds
vectors.why: Negative zero and zero are one number, so they are one spelling.

vectors.name: json-scalars
vectors.why: Integers inside the safe domain, both booleans, and null.

vectors.name: arrays-keep-their-order
vectors.why: Row-shaped data is an array precisely because JCS would sort an object's keys and erase the declared column order (KERNEL-SPEC §8).

vectors.name: control-characters-escape
vectors.why: JCS escapes what JSON requires and nothing else.

vectors.name: non-ascii-stays-raw
vectors.why: JCS emits raw UTF-8 rather than \u escapes, which json.dumps does not do by default.

vectors.name: utf16-key-order-differs-from-codepoint-order
vectors.why: JCS sorts keys by UTF-16 code unit, so a non-BMP key sorts BEFORE a private-use key even though its code point is larger. The intermediate structure's sorted-key order is not the byte order.

vectors.name: float-value
vectors.why: A float anywhere is refused (KERNEL-SPEC §2.1).

vectors.name: float-in-array
vectors.why: Including inside an array.

vectors.name: float-key
vectors.why: Including as a mapping key.

vectors.name: integer-outside-jcs-domain
vectors.why: RFC 8785 has no canonical spelling for an integer above 2^53-1.

vectors.name: unsupported-key-class
vectors.why: A key class with no defined JSON spelling is refused, not guessed.

vectors.name: bytes-value
vectors.why: Bytes are rendered at the seam (base64, KERNEL-SPEC §9), never hashed as a sequence of integers here.

vectors.name: non-finite-decimal
vectors.why: NaN has no JSON spelling and no ordering.

vectors.name: keys-collide-after-coercion
vectors.why: True and 'true' become one key; merging them would drop a value.

vectors.name: keys-collide-after-nfc
vectors.why: The composed and decomposed spellings of one key are one key.
